11. Under Section 17A of P.C. Act which was inserted by Act 16 of 2018, there is a bar on the Police Officer to conduct enquiry, inquiry or investigation into any offence alleged to have been committed by a public Servant where the alleged offence is relatable to recommendation or decision of the Public Servant in discharge of his official functions or duties without the previous approval of the Authorities mentioned in Clause - - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:45706 (a), (b) and (c).

Section 17A of the P.C. Act reads as follows:-
"17A. Enquiry or Inquiry or investigation of offences relatable to recommendations made or decision taken by public servant in discharge of official functions or duties.--
No police officer shall conduct any enquiry or inquiry or investigation into any offence alleged to have been committed by a public servant under this Act, where the alleged offence is relatable to any recommendation made or decision taken by such public servant in discharge of his official functions or duties, without the previous Smt R Leelavathi vs State Of Karnataka on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47606425/

(b) in the case of a person who is or was employed, at the time when the offence was alleged to have been committed, in connection with the affairs of a State, of that Government;
(c) in the case of any other person, of the authority competent to remove him from his office, at the time when the offence was alleged to have been committed:

sentences.text: The objective of the amendment appears to be an effort to protect "Public Servants" from being harassed or victimized.

Any safeguard for protection of bona fide actions of the Officers holding a public post must be invoked appropriately without in any way defeating the very objective by permitting it to act as a shield for a legally wrong act.

13. If cognizable offences are made out, needless to state that law requires an FIR to be registered subject to certain safeguards of a preliminary enquiry as may be required in terms of the observations of the Apex Court in Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh and Others1.

The relevant observations of Apex Court are as follows:-
"120.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, we hold:
120.1. The registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 of the Code, if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence and no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a situation.
120.2.

If the information received does not disclose a cognizable offence but indicates the necessity for an inquiry, a preliminary inquiry may be conducted only to ascertain whether cognizable offence is disclosed or not."

The decision must be taken by the Officer in the capacity as a 'Public Servant'.
If any offence is alleged to have been committed by such Public Servant, previous approval as contemplated under Section 17A of P.C. Act is required to be taken.

In both the Writ Petitions it is the specific case of the respondent Authority that the offence is committed by the petitioners in the context of decision taken by them in their official capacity, abusing the power vested.
15. The decision of granting approval at the requisition of a Police Officer on the ground that the alleged offence may have been committed is by the Authority detailed under Section 17A of P.C. Act.
16. Needless to state that such order must reflect an application of mind.

Interference by a way of judicial review in writ proceedings is to be limited to interfering with the order only when there are mala fides, order is without jurisdiction and when demonstrable extraneous - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:45706 considerations have played a role in the decision making process.

It is essential to keep in mind that judicial review of Executive action can by no stretch of imagination lead to a situation where the Court seeks to substitute its decision with the decision taken by the Executive.
17. It is in such context, the validity of the orders of sanction at Annexures-'B', 'D' and 'F' in W.P.No.19041/2024 and in W.P.No.20592/2024 at Annexure-'H' are required to be examined.

sentences.text: The order of sanction itself narrates the essential facts as detailed supra at paras-19 to 21.
Such decision of sanction cannot be interfered with by calling upon the State to establish a foolproof case at this stage itself.
31. The allegation regarding non-application of mind is liable to be rejected in light of the express order of sanction with reference to material as adverted to hereinabove.

32. The approvals to be taken and entrustment to the C.I.D. are internal matters of the Executive and petitioner cannot question such procedures of investigation - 21 - NC: 2024:KHC:45706 by the State Authorities or its transfer to the C.I.D. at this stage.

33. Though it is contended that the petitioners are not arrayed as accused in the FIR in Crime Nos.0007/2023, 0056/2023 and 0079/2022 with respect to which approval has been granted,
however, that by itself cannot result in construing that petitioner is not involved.

The investigation into a First Information Report may lead to material indicating commission of offence by other persons whose name may eventually be mentioned in the charge-sheet, though not mentioned in the FIR.

34. Insofar as the assertion that no incriminating material was seized during the search, it would not be an appropriate stage to comment upon such assertion as the investigation into IPC offences would by itself not be conclusive as regards offences under P.C. Act.
Even otherwise it would not be appropriate to comment upon the material still to be placed in the form of the chargesheet.

Insofar as the general allegation that the State is 'cherry picking' the accused, it must be observed that such allegation cannot confer any legal benefit on the petitioner and even otherwise the statement of learned Special Public Prosecutor Sri Jagadeesha B.N. that the State would proceed against all accused who are involved in the offence without discrimination is to be accepted in good faith with the State being obligated to proceed against all accused.

36. Considering the stage of the proceedings, the materials placed before the Authority would indicate that the State has made out a case for granting approval under Section 17A of the P.C. Act.
37.
The authorities relied by the petitioner do not in anyway create any further legal obligation upon the State than as has been discharged in the present case as demonstrated.

"17A. Enquiry or Inquiry or investigation of offences relatable to recommendations made or decision taken by public servant in discharge of official functions or duties.--
